title: Size a URL shortener
scenario: A link shortener expects the traffic below. Use 2.6 million seconds per month and decimal units (1 TB = 10¹² bytes). Anything within 25% counts.

questions.prompt: Memory to cache the 10 million most-used links

solution:
1. **Writes:** 100,000,000 ÷ 2,600,000 ≈ **38 per second**. Tiny: one database could take it.
2. **Peak reads:** 100 × 38.5 ≈ 3,850 redirects per second on average, × 3 ≈ **11,500 at peak**. Reads dominate, so caching matters most.
3. **Storage:** 100M × 12 months × 5 years = 6 billion links × 500 bytes = 3 × 10¹² bytes = **3 TB**, about 9 TB with three copies.
4. **Cache:** 10,000,000 × 500 bytes = 5 × 10⁹ bytes = **5 GB**, which fits in the memory of a single cache node (replicate it for availability).
